BEE-ACC-09.say: Here is where three-phase power is born, in 3D: a turbine driving a generator. Look at the stator windings around the spinning rotor. Three sets of coils sit 120 degrees apart, so they make three waves at once. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-DIG-02.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a circuit board. Logic gates live inside chips like the black IC in the middle, joined by copper traces. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-DIG-10.say: Let me show you a real board in 3D. The black IC chip could be a microcontroller, with copper traces carrying signals to its pins, an LED to switch and capacitors to keep its supply steady. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-EMAG-05.say: First, picture the field you are going to move, in 3D: a bar magnet and its field lines. Push it into a coil and the flux through the coil changes, which is exactly what Faraday's law is about. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-01.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a transformer. Look at the iron core, the primary coil on one side and the secondary coil on the other. They never touch; the changing magnetic flux in the core links them. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-02.say: Here is a transformer in 3D. See the thin laminations stacked in the iron core? They cut eddy currents, one of the losses you are about to meet. The copper coils make the other loss. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-03.say: Now let me show you a real DC motor in 3D. Look at the north and south field magnets, the armature winding between them, and the commutator with its carbon brushes. Watch it turn. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-04.say: Here is a DC machine in 3D. Spin this same machine with an engine and it becomes a generator: the armature coils cut the field and a voltage appears at the brushes. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-05.say: First, the real machine in 3D: a DC motor with its field magnets, armature and commutator. Its torque and speed are what the curve in this lesson is about. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-06.say: Now the real thing in 3D: an induction motor, opened up. Look at the stator windings around the outside. Three-phase current in them makes a magnetic field that spins, with nothing moving but electricity. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-07.say: Here is an induction motor in 3D. See the squirrel-cage rotor inside the stator? It is just bars and end rings, with no wires going to it, yet it spins, a little slower than the field. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-08.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a power station's turbine and generator. Steam spins the blades, the coupling turns the generator rotor, and the stator windings deliver the power. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-MACH-10.say: Here is the kind of motor we need to start gently, in 3D: a big induction motor. At standstill its rotor bars draw a huge current, which is why starters exist. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-PWR-01.say: Now let me show you the whole journey in 3D: the power station, the step-up transformer, the pylons and lines, the substation and your home. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-PWR-02.say: Here is the grid in 3D. Follow the transmission lines on the tall pylons: they carry power at very high voltage, and the step-up transformer next to the power station is what makes that possible. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BEE-PWR-10.say: Here is a grid in 3D, from power station to homes. Every generator on it spins in step, and the frequency tells you whether supply and demand are balanced. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-FLUID-09.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a centrifugal pump, cut open. Water enters at the eye, the spinning impeller flings it outwards, and the volute casing slows it down into pressure at the outlet. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-HEAT-06.say: Here is a shell-and-tube heat exchanger in 3D. The hot fluid runs through the tubes, the cold fluid flows around them in the shell, and the baffles make it zigzag for better contact. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-HEAT-10.say: An air conditioner is a refrigeration cycle, so here it is in 3D: compressor, condenser coil, expansion valve and evaporator coil. Heat goes in at one coil and out at the other. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-MACHD-01.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a gear train. Count the teeth on the driver gear and the small gear; that ratio is the whole secret of gear speed and torque. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-MACHD-02.say: Belts and chains are cousins of the pulley, so here is one in 3D. Watch how the rope wraps the wheels and carries the pull from one to the other. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-MACHD-03.say: Here is a ball bearing in 3D, cut open. Look at the outer race, the inner race, and the balls held apart by the cage. Rolling instead of sliding is what keeps friction tiny. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-MFG-05.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a lathe. The chuck spins the workpiece, and the cutting tool on the carriage peels off a thin ribbon of metal. That is turning. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-MFG-07.say: Here is a lathe in 3D. On a CNC lathe, motors turn the lead screw and move the carriage exactly where the G-code tells them, instead of a person turning handwheels. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-SOM-07.say: Now let me show you a beam bending in 3D. The colours show the stress: squashed in compression on top, stretched in tension below, and the neutral axis in between feels nothing. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-SOM-08.say: Here is an I-beam bending in 3D. The thin web in the middle is where most of the shear stress travels, while the flanges carry the bending. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-STAT-03.say: Here is a moment you can see in 3D: a lever on a fulcrum. The effort distance and the load distance decide who wins the turning contest. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-STAT-04.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a truss bridge. Look at the triangles between the top chord and the bottom chord. Every joint is a pin, and that is what lets you solve it joint by joint. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-STAT-05.say: Here is a truss bridge in 3D. Imagine sawing straight through it: the top chord, a diagonal and the bottom chord would each be cut, and those three forces are what the method of sections finds. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-THERM-07.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a petrol engine cylinder. Look at the piston, the valves and the spark plug. The Otto cycle is a simple model of what happens in here. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-THERM-08.say: Here is an engine cylinder in 3D. In a diesel there is no spark plug: the piston squeezes the air so hard it gets hot enough to light the fuel. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-THERM-09.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a steam power plant. Follow the loop: the boiler makes steam, the turbine spins the generator, the condenser turns it back to water, and the feed pump sends it round again. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BME-THERM-10.say: Here is the fridge cycle in 3D. The compressor squeezes the refrigerant, the condenser coil dumps heat, the expansion valve drops the pressure, and the evaporator coil soaks up heat from inside. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-CONC-03.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a reinforced concrete beam, cut open. Look at the main bars low down in the tension zone, the stirrups wrapped around them, and the concrete cover outside. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-CONC-07.say: Here is a steel I-beam bending in 3D. Most of its steel sits in the flanges, far from the neutral axis, which is why its second moment of area is so big for its weight. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-CONC-10.say: Here is a reinforced concrete beam in 3D. See the cover, the layer of concrete outside the bars? It is the steel's raincoat, and this lesson is about keeping it thick enough. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-ENV-01.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a water treatment works. Follow the water from the intake through mixing, flocculation, the settling tank, the sand filter and chlorination to the clear water tank. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-ENV-02.say: Here is a water works in 3D. Look at the flocculation tank and the settling tank next to it: tiny flocs grow, then sink as sludge. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-ENV-03.say: Here is a water works in 3D. The sand filter and the chlorination stage near the end are the last two barriers before the clear water tank. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-GEO-09.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a pile foundation. The column stands on a pile cap, and the piles go down through soft clay and dense sand towards bedrock. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-HYD-05.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a concrete gravity dam. Its huge weight holds back the reservoir. Look at the crest, the gallery inside, and the grout curtain sealing the rock below. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-HYD-06.say: Here is a gravity dam in 3D. See the spillway on its face? In a flood, water pours over it down to the tailwater, and that energy has to be tamed. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-STRA-06.say: Here is a beam deflecting in 3D, between a pin support and a roller support. The bend is exaggerated so you can see it; this lesson works out how big it really is. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-STRA-10.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a suspension bridge. The main cables hang in a curve between the towers, the hangers carry the deck, and the anchorages hold the huge pull at each end. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-SURV-02.say: Here is a modern survey instrument in 3D, the total station: a theodolite with a laser rangefinder built in. Look at the telescope, the tribrach and the levelling screws on the tripod. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-SURV-03.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a total station on its tripod, sending its EDM beam to a reflector prism. It measures the angle and the distance in one go. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-SURV-04.say: Here is the instrument you traverse with, in 3D: a total station. At each station you level it, sight back and forward, and read an angle and a distance. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-TRAN-04.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a road, cut open. Look at the surface course, the binder course, the base, the sub-base and the subgrade underneath. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BCE-TRAN-06.say: Here is a road in 3D. The top two layers, the surface course and the binder course, are the asphalt this lesson is about: stones glued together with bitumen. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BLIT-C18-01.say: Here is the machine that made the novel possible, in 3D: a printing press. Cheap printed books found a growing middle-class readership hungry for stories like Crusoe's. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BLIT-MED-03.say: Here is what Chaucer's readers held, in 3D: a handwritten manuscript on vellum, with a decorated initial, gold leaf and red rubrics. Every copy was made by hand. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BLIT-MED-05.say: Gawain survives in just one handwritten manuscript, so here is a manuscript in 3D: vellum pages, a quill pen, an ink pot and a decorated initial. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BLIT-MED-09.say: Medieval books were copied by hand, like this manuscript in 3D. Julian's and Margery's words reached us through pages like these. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BLIT-REN-01.say: Here is where Hamlet was first played, in 3D: the Globe theatre. Look at the stage jutting into the yard, the galleries around it, and the tiring house where the actors changed. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BLIT-REN-03.say: Here is Shakespeare's Globe in 3D. Standing in the yard cost a penny, and the comedies played on that open stage in daylight. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-ANC-03.say: Now the real thing in 3D: the pyramids of Giza beside the Nile, built in the Old Kingdom. Look at the Great Pyramid, Khafre's pyramid and the Great Sphinx. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-ANC-08.say: Here is Rome at its height in 3D: the Colosseum, opened in AD 80. Look at the arena, the hypogeum beneath it and the seating for tens of thousands. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-ANC-09.say: Here is a wall on the northern frontier in 3D. The Han extended frontier walls to guard the Silk Road, though most of the brick wall standing today was built later, under the Ming. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-C20-02.say: Now let me show you a trench in 3D, as it was on the Western Front. Look at the parapet of sandbags, the fire step, the duckboards, the dugout, and the barbed wire facing no man's land. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-COLD-10.say: Here is the Berlin Wall in 3D. It was not one wall but a system: the border wall, the death strip with its patrol road and floodlights, the watchtower and an inner wall. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-EMOD-01.say: Here is the machine that spread humanist ideas, in 3D: Gutenberg's kind of printing press. Movable type let scholars share accurate texts across Europe. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-EMOD-02.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a printing press. Luther's pamphlets were printed on presses like this in their hundreds of thousands. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-EMOD-03.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a caravel, the small, nimble ship of the Portuguese voyages. Look at the lateen sails that let it sail close to the wind. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-EMOD-04.say: Here is a caravel in 3D. Ships like this carried crops, animals and, without anyone knowing, diseases across the Atlantic. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-METH-02.say: Here is a primary source in 3D: a handwritten medieval manuscript. Ask who wrote it, for whom, and why someone paid for gold leaf on that initial. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

BHIS-REV-06.say: Now the real thing in 3D: a Watt steam engine. Look at the beam, the cylinder, the separate condenser that saved fuel, and the flywheel turning motion into rotation. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
